newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber prices down at noon on Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber prices down at noon on Tokyo.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were down at noon after tracking a weak futures market in Tokyo due to a lack of domestic leads.

At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted benchmark May RSS1 buyer at 290 cents ($1.15) a kg, down half cent from Tuesday's close. April SMR 20 buyer was also half cent lower at 273.50 cents a kg.
Dealers attributed the bearish undertone to uncertainties in Tokyo, saying there were "few parcels of sales here and there" and that the local market was not entirely dead.
An official source said there were 1,000 tonnes of SMR20 sold to South Africa at 272 cents a kg for May shipment.
The source added that there were inquiries from Iran as well for the SMR20.
Traders, however, could not confirm this.
At noon, trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 272 cents a kg, SMR CV at 343, SMR L at 323, SMR 5 at 283, SMR 10 at 273 and drum latex FOB at 232.
